correctness.rationale: For n=N-1 the hypergeometric law has two atoms, and both matching binomial point masses equal the Bin(N,L/N) mass at its integer mean. This yields an exact closed form for the maximal density ratio. Its adjacent quotient on the half-range is C_{N-k-1}/A_k. Strict monotonicity of C_m plus exact inequalities C_{3k+1}<A_k<C_{3k+2} proves H_N(k+1)>H_N(k) iff N>=4k+3, hence the unique half-range optimizer floor((N+1)/4) and exactly two reflected global optimizers. No finite experiment is used for the universal claim.

value.rationale: The leave-one-out regime n=N-1 is the natural opposite endpoint to the primary paper’s half-sample theorem. It exposes a qualitative reversal of the worst population composition from an edge to asymptotic quarter population, while retaining the same maximal-density-ratio approximation criterion. The exact optimizer and peak value therefore give structural information about a canonical finite-population approximation problem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
